verdict: BOUND AS REPORTED, WITH ONE SCOPE STATEMENT. The binary's hash and size match. Its build copy is exactly frozen source 004. It links the exact 71c322c1 C object, whose 347 instructions appear unchanged as _chonk_darwin_spawn_v1. Its Mach-O shape, single libSystem load and 205-symbol import closure match root's report, and all imports resolve in the canonical 8ff49e0c libSystem plus its re-exported libdyld. The managed launch route is one direct chain from the session loop to the C shim. The generic fork/execvp/posix_spawnp imports are not dead: they sit in Rust std's Command implementation, which chonk-shell's generic spawn helpers reach, and those helpers are statically reachable from shared Shell and session code. Only the runtime guards established in my 001-004 source reviews keep the standalone profile from executing them; this binary review does not prove those guards. No runtime approval follows.

An instruction-by-instruction comparison of all 347 instructions shows 0 differences after normalizing the 23 relocated instructions (BRANCH26 calls and the stack-guard GOT_LOAD_PAGE21/PAGEOFF12 loads) and PC-relative branch offsets. Each relocated bl resolves through __stubs to the same import the object names: ___error, ___stack_chk_fail, _close, _fcntl, _posix_spawn, _posix_spawn_file_actions_{init,adddup2,destroy}, _posix_spawnattr_{init,setflags,getflags,setsigdefault,setsigmask,setpgroup,destroy} and _strcmp. The binary's only call to _posix_spawn is inside this function.

spawn_routes.managed_c_route: This is the direct-call chain, and spawn_using<FrozenDarwinShim> has exactly one caller at each level: session_entry::drive<NativeIo>, NativeIo::frame (and Server::deliver_hid), DesktopSession::service, TerminalLauncher::request_from, OwnedApplications::launch_at<FrozenDarwinShim>, spawn_using<FrozenDarwinShim>, _chonk_darwin_spawn_v1, _posix_spawn. There is no spawn_using<UnavailableShim> instantiation and no UnavailableShim symbol.
spawn_routes.residual_process_imports: _posix_spawnp and _fork each have exactly one call site, in std::sys::process::unix Command::spawn. _execvp, _setuid and _chroot each have one, in Command::do_exec (the fork child path). These are Rust std's ordinary Command paths, not the managed shim.
spawn_routes.who_reaches_std_command: In the reverse direct-call graph (bl/b only, depth up to 6), the first crate-level callers of std Command::spawn are: chonk_shell::spawn::spawn_supervised, chonk_shell::spawn::spawn_detached_with_env, the closure in chonk_shell::appearance::apply_to_applications, and the thread body of chonk_shell::omarchy_menu::Evaluator::services.
spawn_routes.static_reachability_from_session: Those helpers are statically reachable from code the native session runs: Shell::run_root_menu_action, run_action_from, run_menu_action and tick; Desktop::tick_menu through OmarchyMenu::tick; DesktopSession::new (the inlined constructor's session-relaunch loop); and through these, DesktopSession::service, Server::deliver_hid, Server::enable_desktop_shell, Server::queue_startup_terminals, desktop_entry::run and NativeIo::frame.
spawn_routes.thread_creation: _pthread_create has one call site, in std Thread::new. Its crate-level callers are chonk_shell Rescanner::tick, OmarchyMenu::tick, the spawn helpers, the omarchy Evaluator::services thread, and the OnceLock initializer for chonk_shell::appearance::propagation::Worker.
spawn_routes.other_signal_use: Shell::apply_session_state_inner calls _kill (signalling running generic terminals when appearance changes). OwnedApplications::poll's kill and waitpid are the managed owner's. Separately, smithay's SHM pool lazily installs a process-global SIGBUS sigaction (place_sigbus_handler), outside the session's managed PIPE/CHLD/INT/TERM/HUP set; this is informational.
spawn_routes.what_keeps_standalone_off_generic_paths: These are source-level runtime guards, established in my reviews of 001-004, not by this artifact review. A managed Shell returns early in run_action_from, run_menu_action, run_root_menu_action and tick. app_rescan is None. The Omarchy menu is never set in standalone. SessionLayout::start_at(None, false, &[]) yields an empty relaunch list. Autostart is gated by !standalone. Appearance changes are refused, and the initialization pass returns before publish/propagate. The direct-call graph cannot show these branch conditions, and indirect (vtable or closure) calls are not in it.

bounded_conclusions: The build copy, binary, C object, Mach-O shape and import closure are bound exactly as root reported.
Managed application launch in this binary goes only through the exact reviewed C shim to posix_spawn (one call site).

Generic Rust std process and thread creation remains linked and statically reachable, so I make no claim that it is absent. Runtime exclusion rests on the reviewed standalone guards. The closed60 run should treat any child process or thread-driven external effect it cannot attribute to a managed instance as a failure. An end-of-run process listing or the app records showing only the managed PIDs would corroborate that, but is not required by this review.
